title: Does Sitting All Day at the Office Make You Gain Weight? Here's How to Balance It
intro: Sitting by itself doesn't turn into fat, but sitting for long hours all day means your body burns less energy. The good news is, small movements throughout the day can help balance things out.

sections.h: The real problem: the daily movement you've lost
sections.p: The energy your body uses every day doesn't come from exercise alone. Walking, standing, taking the stairs and doing housework also add up a lot. Office work and WFH make these small movements almost disappear.

Get up every 45 to 60 minutes, even for just 2 minutes. Refill your own water, use the toilet that's further away and take the stairs for one or two floors. If you have a call without a screen, take it while walking.

sections.h: Eating at your desk and meeting kuih
sections.p: Eating while looking at a screen makes us less aware of when we're actually full. Snacks on the desk are also easy to grab without thinking. You can enjoy meeting kuih, just pick one you really like and eat it slowly.

If you WFH, replace your commute time with a 15-minute walk in the morning or evening. If you do field work and spend a lot of time in the car, stretch and walk a bit every time you stop. Tired after traffic? A short 15-minute workout at home is already good enough.

action: Set an alarm every hour to get up and move for 2 to 3 minutes.
Use a small water bottle so you have to get up to refill it more often.
Walk for 10 minutes after lunch, even if it's just around the building.
Keep snacks in a drawer or the pantry, not on your desk.
Check your average daily steps and try to add 1,000 steps this week.
myth: Many people think that if they've gone to the gym for an hour, sitting for 9 hours is no big deal. Exercise is great, but movement throughout the day also contributes a lot to the total energy you burn. Both are important.

faq.q: How many steps a day should I aim for?
faq.a: There's no magic number. Start with your current average and add a little at a time. For many people, 7,000 to 8,000 steps is a reasonable target.

faq.q: Can a standing desk help with weight loss?
faq.a: It can help a little, but standing still in one place isn't much different from sitting. What matters more is moving often and changing positions.

faq.q: How do I handle kuih and sweet drinks during meetings?
faq.a: Take one kuih you like the most, put it on a plate and eat it slowly. Pair it with plain water or less-sweet tea, and no need to feel guilty.
